messages:
Harper T.: hey all, Harper here (first day!). I ran `kubectl config get-contexts` and only see `minikube`. I need read on `staging` and a personal ns `harper-onboard` to try infra examples. Who do I ping and what should I include in the ticket? :wave:

Nina (DevEx): welcome Harper! :tada: open an infra ticket and include your corp email, manager, desired namespaces and perms (read/write), and paste `kubectl config view --minify --flatten`. That lets infra merge your kubeconfig.

Harper T.: pasted kubeconfig below (very small):
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts: []
current-context: minikube
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: minikube
```

I created INF-999 and linked @dave_m as my manager.

onboard-bot: ticket INF-999 created and assigned to eng-infra. https://tickets.redwood/INF-999

Eli (Eng-Infra): hey Harper  we usually create `onboard-<name>` ns and bind `edit` there, and add you to `redwood-staging-read`. I'll provision now. If you need staging write, request temporary elevation and include an expiry.

Eli (Eng-Infra): done  rolebindings applied. Can you run these to verify:
```
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=harper-onboard
kubectl auth can-i create deployments --namespace=staging
```

Harper T.: ran them  contexts now include `redwood-staging` and `harper-onboard`, `auth can-i` yes for list in my ns and no for create in staging (that's fine). I can deploy a test pod in my namespace. Thanks! :raised_hands:

Nina (DevEx): nice! Two tips: 1) switch context with `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging` and 2) if your kubeconfig gets noisy do `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config && chmod 600 ~/.kube/config`. Ping if anything else.
